Ruling

The judge's explanation, as written

To both parties. The SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02706 is refunded in full to the rider. No driver compensation is payable. The monetary effect is SGD 4.50, at or below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so the refund executes on issue. Why the charge cannot stand. A no-show fee is chargeable only if every limb of POL-NS-01 holds, and limb (c) does not. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, EV-TRIP-02706). Measured the way POL-NS-01(c) requires — from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the arrival tap — the driver held position for 67 seconds, from 12:51:17 to 12:52:24 (longest qualifying in-geofence run, EV-GPS-02706), and the platform's own wait timer agrees, running from 12:51:19 to the 12:52:28 termination. That is a shortfall of 113 seconds. Limb (d) fails on the same arithmetic, because the termination did not fall at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed. POL-NS-06 then refunds the cancellation-fee line in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider answered messages. The shortfall cannot be bridged. POL-NS-06(i) allows separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a qualifying traffic advisory covers the pickup road; this trace shows a single in-geofence interval (run_count 1), and the only advisory artifact on file, EV-ADVIS-02706-01, is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so no accumulation is available and no advisory can be asserted for either party. The driver's claims. (1) Arrival on admissible fixes: accepted. The trace carries 8 qualifying in-radius fixes on a complete 10-second, 100%-coverage trace, so POL-NS-01 limb (b) is met — but limb (b) alone does not make the fee chargeable. (2) The 'I'm Here' tap is a genuine marker, not a POL-NS-05 false marker: accepted; the tap coincides with the first qualifying in-geofence fix (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0), so no false-arrival referral is entered. (3) Limb (d)'s reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW is one of the three the limb recognises: accepted, but limb (d) also requires termination at or after the elapsed dwell, which fails. (4) POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider because the driver replied 'ok' within 120 seconds: this is outcome-neutral. Even if the driver is right that his 12:52:32 reply defeats POL-NS-04, the refund flows from POL-NS-06 independently, so the point decides nothing and I do not need to resolve it. (5) No anti-farming concern: accepted, and POL-GEN-01 is respected — the citable trailing-30-day figure is 0 against 107 completed trips, the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter is not substituted for it, and no other profile field is used to ground any finding about this trip. (6) The 113-second shortfall: accepted, and it is decisive. The rider's claims. (1) 180 seconds in force, 69 seconds on the platform timer: accepted. (2) 67-second GPS-derived run, 113-second shortfall: accepted. (3) Limb (c) and limb (d) both fail: accepted. (4) No accumulation, advisory missing: accepted. (5) The rider's device sat 13.15 m to 19.08 m from the pin across the whole window: accepted as far as it goes, but it is not needed — POL-NS-06 refunds irrespective of rider presence, so the driver's counterparty statement that the rider 'was not visible' does not change the result. That statement carries no weight_multiplier and forms no part of the confidence cap. The driver's further reason, that he had another booking waiting, is not a ground POL-NS-06 recognises. (6) Relief: accepted — SGD 4.50 is the cancellation-fee line actually charged (EV-FARE-02706, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), and that is the whole of the contested amount. Confidence is 0.95. The deciding fact — the shortfall against the 180-second waiting period — is carried by EV-GPS-02706 and EV-TRIP-02706, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, and neither is impaired under POL-NS-08. The missing advisory carries no deciding fact and does not lower the cap. Referrals: none. No clause produces one. The arrival marker was genuine, so POL-NS-05(ii) does not fire; the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check is not tripped; and no POL-NS-09 trigger applies (confidence is above the 0.70 floor, no admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence, the parties have no trailing-90-day dispute history, and no deciding artifact is impaired). The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

How to appeal: Either party may appeal once within 30 days. A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

confidence 0.95floor 0.7 (POL-GEN-02)

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 4.50 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It does not exceed the threshold, so the amount is executed automatically on issue, subject to POL-GEN-04.

The rider advocate

kept The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds, read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec (the record carries platform_policy, so the fee_schedule defaults are not reached). The platform's own waiting timer started at 12:51:19 and the driver terminated the trip at 12:52:28 — 69 seconds later, 111 seconds short of the period the fee buys. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable on an effective dwell shorter than that period, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded; the driver's stated reason for cancelling, that he had another booking waiting, is not a ground that clause recognises.

evidence EV-TRIP-02706 · clauses POL-NS-06, POL-NS-01

kept Independently of the platform's timer, the GPS-derived arrival facts measure the driver's longest continuous qualifying in-geofence run at 67 seconds, running from 12:51:17 to 12:52:24 over 8 fixes, against a STANDARD minimum dwell of 180 seconds — a shortfall of 113 seconds. POL-NS-01(c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the 'I'm Here' tap, and the derived dwell_start_offset_sec of 0.0 shows the two coincide here, so the driver cannot gain time from the marker.

evidence EV-GPS-02706, EV-TRIP-02706 · clauses POL-NS-06, POL-NS-01

kept POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and the rider wins by breaking a single limb. Limb (c) fails because the driver held position inside the geofence for 67 seconds, not the 180 seconds in force, and limb (d) fails because the trip was terminated at 12:52:28, before the required dwell had elapsed — limb (d) requires termination at or after the moment that dwell elapses. The reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW being one of the three codes limb (d) recognises does not save the charge where the dwell condition in limb (c) is not met.

evidence EV-TRIP-02706, EV-GPS-02706 · clauses POL-NS-01

kept The 113-second shortfall cannot be closed by accumulation. The derived arrival facts report run_count of 1, so there is no second in-geofence interval for POL-NS-06(i) to add to the first, and the only traffic advisory artifact on the file, EV-ADVIS-02706-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — no advisory covers the pickup road in this window, which is why limb (i) is unavailable to the driver. No shortfall can be made up out of an advisory that does not exist.

evidence EV-GPS-02706, EV-ADVIS-02706-01 · clauses POL-NS-06

The driver's counterparty statement that the rider 'was not visible' is not supported by the platform's own telemetry of the rider's device at the pin.

evidence EV-GPS-02706, EV-TRIP-02706 · clauses POL-NS-04

kept POL-NS-04's other two limbs are made out. Limb (a): the rider sent a locating, coordinating message during the waiting window — 'im at the lobby, coming out', sent 12:52:17, delivered 12:52:18. Limb (b): the driver posted his only message, 'ok', at 12:52:32, four seconds AFTER he terminated the trip at 12:52:28, and the rider's message was not read until 12:52:37; nothing was posted before termination, and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, so no in-app call was placed either. I note that POL-NS-04's closing sentence treats a reply within 120 seconds as defeating the clause, and that the rider's case does not depend on this point: the 113-second dwell shortfall under POL-NS-06 refunds the fee in any event.
